Commentary.Commentary: Brisbane done, off to Canberra next but Sri Lanka have a baggage of an injury as well along with the defeat to be carried forward. Lahiru Kumara is ruled out of the series. Lots of headaches for the visitors and one can only think that the only way for them to come back will be to start afresh and treat the next one as a completely new game, trying to forget this loss as soon as possible. That Test will begin on 1st Feb, Friday. That will be a Day game and will begin at 1030 Local (2330 GMT, Jan 31 night). Join us for that! Till then, take care and cheers. For live cricketing action now though, you can switch tabs to follow the game between India and New Zealand where the hosts are chasing a mountain of runs at Mount Maunganui.
PAT CUMMINS IS ADJUDGED AS THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS INCREDIBLE MATCH FIGURES OF 10/62.

Earlier in the game, Australia bundled out the visitors for a paltry 144 after the latter had won the toss and decided to bat first. Cummins was the wrecker-in-chief in that innings as well picking up four whereas the debutant Jhye picked up three. In their turn to bat, Australia were at a precarious position at one stage at 82/4 but then a 166-run stand for the fifth wicket between Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head meant they comfortably went past the Sri Lankan total. They ended up with a lead of 179 which in the end proved to be more than enough for the hapless Asian team.

Sri Lanka have received a real pasting here. Outplayed in all departments in this Daynight Test here at Brisbane. The second innings went spiralling down and the lack of resistance would be what hurts the visitors the most. Pat Cummins destroyed the batting order picking up 6 wickets and was given good support by Jhye Richardson who picked up two of his own. Nathan Lyon had a lone wicket whereas the last batsman, Lahiru Kumara was absent hurt. There was not much to talk about the batting, only Lahiru Thirimanne provided some resistance but was running out of partners all through the innings.

Jhye Richardson in an interview says that he was nervous the first day. Adds that he is happy to have contributed to the team victory. Applauds his teammates for a stellar performance and singles out Cummins for special praise. Talking about the post-match huddle, he says that the skipper was telling them that it was a pep talk and motivation for them to continue these kind of performances. Signs off by saying it was an amazing catch from Patterson and really loves the fielding effort of everyone.

OUT! It is all over here at the 'Gabba. Lahiru Kumara is not going to come out to bat and hence, that is the end of the Test match. AUSTRALIA HAVE WON BY AN INNINGS AND 40 RUNS, LEAD 1-0 IN THE TWO-MATCH SERIES. Coming to the last wicket, it was a flighted ball on middle and turning in, Lakmal could not resist and comes down the ground looking to smash it into oblivion but misses the ball and Paine completes an easy stumping. A fitting way for the inspirational skipper of Australia to end the game. He took over in tough times and this victory would mean a lot after the series loss to India. Pulls up all the teammates in a huddle and gives a pep talk before they walk off the field all smiles.

OUT! Bizarre! The third umpire asks the umpire to stay with the original decision. What has happened here? The Snicko has shown a turbulence but in a frame that is after the ball passes the bat. It is the fifth wicket for Cummins, the fourth time in Tests. A length ball outside off and shapes away slightly, Thirimanne was ahead to defend but the ball straightens and there is a noise as the ball passes the bat and goes to Tim Paine. An immediate celebration from the fielders and the bowlers and the umpire agrees too. Lahiru was surprised and immediately goes upstairs. The replays roll in, there is nothing on Hotspot and we go to the Snickometer. The line remains straight as the ball passes the outside edge but there is a slight turbulence once it is past the willow. The third umpire feels that the frame was a little behind and suggests it is a faint edge. Asks the on-field umpire to remain with his original decision. Thirimanne cannot believe it but he has to go. His dogged resistance comes to an end. The Lankans are still 100 runs behind with only 4 wickets left.

Review time... Thirimanne has been ruled caught behind by the umpire but he has taken it upstairs as he thinks that he has not nicked that one. Does not look too confident though. Let's see what the replays say.

Welcome back after Tea. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Lahiru Thirimanne and Niroshan Dickwella are out as well. Mitchell Starc will bowl the first over of this session and Thirimanne will face.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Now, Niroshan Dickwella has joined forces with the opening batsman. They played out one remaining over of the session but whether they will continue and help Sri Lanka out of this mess and keep them alive in the game is to be seen. Doesn't look like they will to me though, considering how Cummins and Richardson are bowling. The former has got enough rest after his initial burst in the first session and should be back on anytime now after the break. Good luck to the Sri Lankan batsmen, would be lovely for Test cricket if they stand up and post a challenge though. Join us in a bit for the second session of the day as the visitors try to wipe off the deficit that is still 105 runs.

What a session for the Aussies but one would have definitely hoped for a bit more of a fight from the Lankans. 26 overs, 57 runs and 4 wickets. No boundary off the bat. Guess who has been the star? Yes, it is that man again. Pat Cummins. Started off from where he left off last night and picked up three more wickets this morning. Lahiru Thirimanne has been adamant not to give his wicket away and even though DRS came to his rescue once, other times he has looked completely solid. No one partnered him though and just when it looked like Dhananjaya would stay he was castled off a brilliant yorker length ball by Jhye Richardson.

Thirimanne survives, some positive news for the Lankans. Lyon cannot believe it though and seems to suggest that he did not think that one would bounce over the wickets.

Full on middle, Thirimanne flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen pick up a couple.
A good short ball on middle, fended off towards the leg side by Thirimanne. Gets to the other end and keeps strike for the next over.
Slightly shortens the length this time, Lahiru stands in his crease and defends it back down the ground.
Good, positive defensive stroke from LT towards mid off.
A length ball outside off, Thirimanne comes ahead and dead-bats this one.
A length ball shaping away from the left-hander, Lahiru goes for the drive but fails to put bat on ball.
Fuller one on the pads, flicked away to the square leg region by Thirimanne for a couple of runs.
Good length delivery on leg, Silva looks to push but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Third consecutive leave for Roshen Silva. Good length delivery again outside off, Roshen offers no shot.
Again outside off, Silva lets it go.
Good rise on this delivery. Good length delivery outside off, Silva shoulders his arms to this one.
Again on a good length  on off, Roshen defends off the back foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Silva leaves it alone.
Back to over the wicket, angling away from the left-hander. Thirimanne prods ahead and pushes this one to mid off.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to duck under it and evade.
Sprays this one down the leg side, the ball takes the pad as it passes the batsman. It is a good collection from Paine down the leg side.
Good, solid defense as the straight bat is presented by Lahiru.
Length ball once more on top of off stump, kept out by the lefty coming half-ahead.
Around the wicket, Thirimanne comes ahead and defends with a straight bat.
A length ball on middle, kept out by Roshen.
Oooh...another outside edge but good technique from Silva as he removes his bottom hand and ensures the ball goes all along the ground to the slip cordon.
A length ball on off, Thirimanne comes forward and turns it away off the inside half of the bat towards the leg side for a single.
Around the wicket to the southpaw, Lahiru comes ahead a bit and then defends the ball.

On the pads this time, flicked away to deep square leg. Roshen gets off the mark straightaway with a triple. Good running that, even though Thirimanne had to rush in the end to make his ground. These are also the first runs off Cummins. He had three wickets for 0 runs, quite incredible!
Roshen Silva comes in next.

OUT! Poor from Mendis! Really poor. A fuller length ball outside off and after missing two balls from Cummins in the previous over, this one takes the outside edge and it goes to Joe Burns at second slip at a good height. He is not dropping those. Cummins is elated and why not, he has three now in three overs. Australia have started off brilliantly here but this is not very good stuff from SL. Need to show some fight!
Comes from around the wicket. Length delivery on off, Thirimanne defends off the front foot.
Bowls a bouncer, Lahiru does well to duck under it.
Good length delivery on off, Thirimanne defends off the back foot.
Length delivery on middle, Mendis flicks it towards the leg side for a single.
Good length delivery on off, Chandimal defends off the front foot.
Full outside off, Thirimanne pushes it wide of mid off for a single.
Another play and a miss! A lovely over from Cummins comes to an end. Shape on this final delivery takes the ball away from Kusal again and he is beaten on the outside.
Outside off on a length and it shapes away to beat the outside edge of Mendis who was playing inside the line.
A length ball on the pads, Mendis misses the flick and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Down the leg side and too wide for the batsman to make any contact.
Kusal Mendis walks in at number 4.

OUT! Brute of a delivery! Off the top of the bat and to Kurtis Patterson at gully. Chandimal bags a duck. A length ball on off stump and it rises too much suddenly, the ball has too much spice and Chandimal tries to defend it on the off side but to his dismay, the ball takes the shoulder of the bat and lobs up towards gully. Patterson jumps and takes a good catch. Two wickets in the space of 3 balls for Cummins, lovely bowling! Sri Lanka have lost their second and this is a very early blow.
Slightly short of a length outside off, left alone by Chandimal.
Pat Cummins to bowl from the other end.
A length ball outside off and a good solid defense from the lefty. Maiden to start off.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it and lets it go.
Gets this one to shape in slightly off a length and the ball is kept out towards mid on by Thirimanne.
Oooh... gets this one slightly close to the off stump, Lahiru prods ahead and gets a thick outside edge towards the gully.
Left alone by the southpaw once more.
A length ball outside off from Jhye, left alone by Thirimanne.

The players are out in the middle. Dinesh Chandimal has come out to join Lahiru Thirimanne. The Aussies are in a huddle. A bit of a tradition is being followed, with a particular celebration for Australia Day. All set to resume play now as the players spread out. 162 behind are the Lankans. Jhye Richardson it will be, to start off proceedings for the day. to Thirimanne. Here we go then... Let's play!

What can the Lankans do from here on? Take inspiration from Windies and England and fight. Battle hard. There is plenty of time left in this Test and the pitch is not a minefield. Application will be the key. To give context in the Windies-England Test, 8 wickets fell on Day 1, 18 on Day 2, but - NONE ON DAY 3. If Sri Lanka manage to do what Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich did yesterday or what VVS Laxman and Rahul Dravid did way back in 2001 at Eden Gardens, boy - we could have a game on our hands. Hello and a warm welcome to the third day's play of the first Test between Australia and Sri Lanka at the 'Gabba.

A look at the scorecard and one would say, it has been Australia's Test so far. They dismantled the Lankans quickly on Thursday and have finished Friday with a lead of 179 and nipped out Karunaratne. But what the scorecard does not show is - opportunities missed by the Lankans. They bowled out of their skins yesterday afternoon, reducing the Aussies to 82/4 as early as the first hour but then lost patience as the heat took toll. Eventually, the Labuschagne-Head stand took the game away from them. That partnership was worth 166, 22 more than what Sri Lanka themselves got.

Now, a warm thanks to all those who have come over to follow this game, considering that an interesting New-Zealand India contest is enveloping at the Bay Oval. This is the third day of this Test and often, Day 3 is considered to be a moving day of cricket. 12 wickets fell on Day 1, 9 on Day 2. Will another 9 fall today and end this game?

'No matter where our personal stories began. Reflect on being Australian, celebrate contemporary Australia and recognize our history.' This is the importance of today. January 26. AUSTRALIA DAY. The date of January 26, 1788 marked the proclamation of British sovereignty over the eastern seaboard of Australia, although the country got its name in 1808. On New Year's Day 1901, the British colonies of Australia formed a federation, marking the birth of modern Australia.  It was not until 1935 that all Australian states and territories adopted use of the term 'Australia Day' to mark the date, and not until 1994 that the date was consistently marked by a public holiday on that day by all states and territories. So to all those reading, WISH YOU A VERY HAPPY AUSTRALIA DAY.
... DAY 3, AFTERNOON SESSION ...

Tough couple of days for Sri Lanka. Bowled out under 60 overs in the first innings, conceded more than 250 on Day 2 and have their backs to the wall at the moment. They still trail by 162 runs with 9 wickets in hand. The middle order needs to step up. Join us at 1 pm local (0300 GMT) on Saturday which is a special day for the Aussies. It is AUSTRALIA DAY and might well be the final day of this Test. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

6 overs were all that Australia got and Tim Paine employed 4 bowlers. Starc sprayed the ball to all parts while Nathan Lyon almost got a wicket. But the star was Pat Cummins who mixed his lines and lengths well and got the wicket.

What is happening? The umpires are having a chat with Tim Paine and Travis Head. The former is smiling but the latter seems very serious. Was there something said to someone? Any sledging? We don't know. Might come in the papers tomorrow. For now, it is Australia's wonderful finish to the day.

OUT! Caught behind! A wicket does fall in the small passage of play! Guess who gets it. Guess who gets it? Not Starc. But that warhorse Pat Cummins. What a beautiful set up in this over. Mixing his lengths, then the lines. Got the ball to come back in and then move away. The last one came back in, this one moved away. Karunaratne was not sure whether to play at that or not and had a push. Got the nick. End of story as Tim Paine did the rest. STUMPS ON DAY 2, SRI LANKA TRAIL BY 162!
Lovely ball. This one shapes back in, from outside off, DK looks to push away from his body but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, Dimuth looks to tap and run to the off side but then Thirimanne is not going anywhere.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne feels for it but then withdraws his bat at the last moment.
Beaten! Has that hit a crack? On a length outside off, Karunaratne feels for the ball outside off but it suddenly seams away and beats the outside edge.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Pat Cummins to bowl one final over probably, before Stumps.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

CHANCE! MISSED! FOUR! Chance gone abegging! Tossed up on off, Thirimanne looks to defend but gets beaten by the turn. He gets an outside edge towards first slip where Khawaja is slow to get to his left and misses it. It goes towards third man for a boundary.
Short on off, Karunaratne cuts it towards point for a single.
Full and around off, big turn, Karunaratne watchfully patted towards point.
Where is the herd? Time for some grazing. For here comes the GOAT... Nathan Lyon to try and see whether he can pick up a wicket.
Outside off, pushed to point for a quick single.
Good length delivery on middle, Thirimanne looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It goes towards fine leg. The batsmen take a run.
Same delivery, Lahiru easily keeps it out.
Good length delivery on off, Thirimanne blocks it off the back foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a length outside off, left alone.

ALMOST A WICKET! Mix-up between the batsmen. Thirimanne pushes this towards mid on and calls for a quick single. The fielder charges in and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Thirimanne might have been in...
Good length delivery on off, Thirimanne defends off the back foot.
On a length outside off, comes back in, Lahiru misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.

FOUR BYES! He bowls to the left, he bowls to the right... remember this song? Starc is reminding us of THAT guy... a certain Mitchell GUY Johnson. Very poor delivery from Starc. Bowls way outside leg, Thirimanne looks to flick but misses it. It goes past Tim Paine who dives in vain to his right.
That is the line. That is the Starc we know. Full and just outside off, swinging in, Thirimanne plays that late and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Down the leg side, total waste of this new strawberry. Easy work for Thirimanne. Watches it go past.
Outside off, Karunaratne lets it go.
Length delivery on middle, Dimuth defends off the back foot.
Full on middle, flicked straight to square leg.
Good shape on this one. Good length delivery outside off, Karunaratne looks to leave it alone but gets hit on the thigh pad as it nips back in sharply.
Good length delivery outside off, Karunaratne shoulders his arms to this one.
On a good length around middle and leg, defended to the leg side. There is a short leg in place.
Jhye Richardson to bowl from the other end.
Full outside off, Thirimanne looks to drive but gets beaten on this one.
Good length delivery on off, Thirimanne defends off the back foot.
Now exploring the other side. Full and miles outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Bowls down the leg side, Karunaratne lets it go.
FOUR LEG BYES! Starts with a poor delivery. Bowls down the leg side, Karunaratne looks to flick but gets it off his pads. It beats the keeper and goes towards fine leg for a boundary.
